0.text: The process begins when the GO starts and requests the measurements from the MSP. The MSP receives this request and checks it. Based on this check, either the MSP denies the GO’s request, after which the process concludes, or the MSP proceeds to perform the measurement. After performing the measurement, either a failure is identified and the MSP informs the GO about the failure, leading the process toward completion, or the measurement succeeds and the MSP transmits the measured values to the GO. The GO then processes these values, sends any changed values back to the MSP, and subsequently transmits the readings to the SP. After either the denial, the failure notification, or the completion of transmitting the readings to the SP, the process ends.

1.text: The process starts in GO when measurements are requested from the MSP. The MSP then checks the received request and decides how to proceed: either the request of the GO is denied, which leads straight to the closing of the process, or the measurement is performed. After performing the measurement, the MSP either informs the GO about the failure or transmits the measured values to the GO. If measured values are transmitted, GO processes the measured values, sends the changed values back to the MSP, and then transmits the readings to the SP. Both the failure notification path and the path that ends with transmitting the readings to the SP converge to the same closing step, after which the process ends.

2.text: The process starts in the GO lane, where the GO requests the measurements to the MSP. The MSP then checks the received request. Based on this check, either the MSP denie the request of the GO and the process proceeds toward completion, or the MSP performs the measurement. After performing the measurement, either the MSP inform the GO about the failure, or the MSP transmit the measured values to the GO. If the values are transmitted, the GO process the measured values, then send the changed values to the MSP, after which the MSP transmit the readings to the SP. Whether the MSP informed the GO about the failure or transmitted the readings to the SP, the flow converges and the process ends.

3.text: The process starts when GO requests the measurements to the MSP. MSP then checks the received request and decides how to proceed: it either denie the request of the GO, or it performs the measurement. If the measurement is performed, a further decision is taken: in case of a failure, MSP informs the GO about the failure; otherwise, MSP transmits the measured values to the GO, after which GO processes the measured values, sends the changed values to the MSP, and then transmits the readings to the SP. The path where GO was informed about a failure and the path where the readings were transmitted to the SP join together, and this combined path then joins with the path where MSP denied the request, after which the process ends.

4.text: The process starts in the GO area, where a request for measurements is issued to the MSP. The MSP then checks the received request and decides how to proceed: either the request is denied, in which case a denial is issued and the process moves toward its conclusion, or the MSP continues and performs the measurement. After performing the measurement, the MSP evaluates the outcome. If there is a failure, the MSP informs the GO about the failure, after which the process heads toward completion. If the measurement succeeds, the MSP transmits the measured values to the GO. The GO then processes these values, sends the changed values back to the MSP, and subsequently transmits the readings to the SP. Following either the failure notification path or the successful exchange and forwarding of readings, the process converges and ends.

5.text: The process begins in GO, where the need arises and GO requests the measurements from MSP. MSP receives this request and checks it. Based on this check, either the request is denied or the work proceeds with performing the measurement. If the request is denied, this outcome is recorded and the process concludes. If the measurement is carried out, the result leads to one of two paths: either MSP detects a failure and informs GO about the failure, or MSP proceeds by transmitting the measured values to GO. When measured values are transmitted, GO processes these values, then sends back changed values to MSP, and subsequently forwards the resulting readings to the SP. Whether GO has been informed about a failure or has transmitted the readings to the SP, the process then converges to a common closure and ends.

6.text: The process begins when the GO requests the measurements from the MSP. The MSP checks the received request and then either denies the GO’s request or proceeds to perform the measurement. If the measurement is carried out, the MSP either informs the GO about a failure or transmits the measured values to the GO. When the GO receives the measured values, it processes them, sends the changed values back to the MSP, and then transmits the readings to the SP. Whether the request was denied, a failure was communicated, or the readings were sent to the SP, the process then converges and ends.

7.text: The process starts in GO, where a request to perform measurements is initiated and sent to MSP. MSP first checks the received request and then decides whether to proceed or not. If MSP decides to deny the request of the GO, the process advances directly to the final consolidation and ends. If MSP decides to proceed, MSP performs the measurement and then evaluates the outcome. If there is a failure, MSP informs the GO about the failure and the process moves to the final consolidation. If the measurement succeeds, MSP transmits the measured values to the GO. GO then processes the measured values, sends the changed values back to the MSP, and subsequently transmits the readings to the SP. After either the failure notification path or the successful processing and transmission path, the flows merge and the process ends.

The MSP then checks the received request and decides whether to denie the request of the GO or to perform the measurement. If the request is denied, the process moves toward completion. If the measurement is performed, the MSP then decides whether to inform the GO about the failure or to transmit the measured values to the GO. 0.text: The customer process starts when the customer perceives a service degradation and informs the telecom provider; on the provider side, Customer Service receives the problem parameters list, enters a problem report into the system, compares it against the customer’s SLA, and determines the necessary countermeasures. The case then loops through determining the customer significance and assessing the significance level: if it is of a certain significance, it returns to refine the determination; otherwise, it proceeds to a further significance-level decision where, for premium customers, it links to an extra problem fix process and then continues, and for other customers it proceeds directly. In both cases, Customer Service creates a detailed problem report and sends it to Service Management. Service Management deals with violations of quality and investigates the problem, then decides whether it is a Service Management problem: if yes, it performs the analysis and creates a trouble report; if no, it sends the problem report to Resource Provisioning, which checks for potential issues, decides whether a problem is detected, and either analyzes the problem and creates a trouble report (if detected) or creates a service execution notification (if not). Resource Provisioning reports status to Service Management, which consolidates inputs and prepares the final status report, then decides which actions are required. If there is no problem, Customer Service sends the actual service performance to Customer Service operations, which receives it and routes the case to a decision that leads to performing two activities in parallel: creating a report for the customer and reporting any SLA violation rebate to Billing & Collections; Billing & Collections adjusts the billing, and once both the customer report and billing adjustment are ready, the case synchronizes and the customer report is sent to the customer, ending the provider’s process. If minor corrective actions are required, Service Management undertakes corrective actions, then routes the case to create a problem resolution report, sends that report to Customer Service, which receives it and routes to the same decision that triggers the same two parallel activities (customer report creation and, if applicable, SLA rebate handling) before sending the customer report and ending. If automatic resource restoration is required, Service Management creates a request for automatic resource restoration and sends it to Resource Provisioning; Resource Provisioning receives the restoration request, tracks all possible errors, undertakes all necessary corrective actions, creates a troubleshooting report, sends it to Service Management, which forwards the troubleshooting report to Customer Service and again routes to create the problem resolution report, send it to Customer Service, and follow the same downstream path to produce the customer report (and any SLA rebate) and finish. On the customer side, after the initial notification, the customer later receives the report from the provider and completes their process.
